ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, an isosceles right-angled triangle object $ABC$ is leaning against a corner of the wall ($\angle O = 90^\circ$). If $OA = 50cm$ and $OB = 28cm$, what is the distance in $cm$ of point $C$ from the ground?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $CD \perp OB$ at point D, as shown in the diagram:\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CDB=\angle AOB=90^\circ$\\
$\because$ $\triangle ABC$ is an isosceles right triangle\\
$\therefore$ AB=CB, $\angle ABC=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABO+\angle CBD=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABO=\angle BCD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ABO\cong \triangle BCD(AAS)$\\
$\therefore$ CD=BO=\boxed{28\text{cm}}

raw_record.standard_answer:
Draw $CD \perp OB$ at point $D$, as shown in the diagram:
$\therefore\ \angle CDB = \angle AOB = 90^\circ$
$\because\ \triangle ABC$ is an isosceles right triangle
$\therefore\ AB = CB$, $\angle ABC = 90^\circ$
$\therefore\ \angle ABO + \angle CBD = 90^\circ$

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the wall and ground meet at O at a right angle; A lies on the vertical wall, B lies on the horizontal ground, and C is the free vertex of triangle ABC above the ground. Drop a perpendicular from C to the ground line OB, meeting it or its extension at D, so the desired distance from C to the ground is CD. From the text read OA = 50 cm, OB = 28 cm, and triangle ABC is an isosceles right triangle with the right angle at B, so AB = CB and ∠ABC = 90°. Use angle chasing: since AO ⟂ OB and CD ⟂ OB, ∠AOB = ∠CDB = 90°. Also ∠ABO + ∠CBD = 90° because AB ⟂ CB, while ∠CBD + ∠BCD = 90° in right triangle BCD, so ∠ABO = ∠BCD. Then triangles ABO and BCD are congruent by AAS together with AB = CB. Therefore CD = BO = 28 cm.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a coordinate setup: take the corner O as the origin, the ground OB as the positive x-axis, and the wall OA as the positive y-axis. From the text read OA = 50 cm and OB = 28 cm, so A = (0,50) and B = (28,0). ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, an isosceles right-angled triangle object $ABC$ is leaning against a corner of the wall ($\angle O = 90^\circ$). If $OA = 50\text{ cm}$ and $OB = 28\text{ cm}$, what is the distance in cm of point $C$ from the ground?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
Draw $CD \perp OB$ at point $D$, as shown in the diagram:
$\therefore\ \angle CDB = \angle AOB = 90^\circ$
$\because\ \triangle ABC$ is an isosceles right triangle
$\therefore\ AB = CB$, $\angle ABC = 90^\circ$
$\therefore\ \angle ABO + \angle CBD = 90^\circ$
$\therefore\ \angle ABO = \angle BCD$
$\therefore\ \triangle ABO \cong \triangle BCD\ (AAS)$
$\therefore\ CD = BO = \boxed{28\text{ cm}}$

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left side is a vertical wall, and the bottom is horizontal ground; the two form a right angle at point O; point A is on the wall, point B is on the ground, point C is on the right side and above the ground, and ABC forms a triangle leaning obliquely at the wall corner. The problem gives OA = 50 cm, OB = 28 cm, and states that △ABC is an isosceles right triangle. Reasoning: From C, draw a perpendicular to the line OB where the ground lies, with foot D; then the distance from C to the ground is CD. Because AO ⟂ OB, and CD ⟂ OB, ∠AOB = ∠CDB = 90°. Also because △ABC is an isosceles right triangle, and the right angle is at B, AB = CB, ∠ABC = 90°. From AB ⟂ CB, ∠ABO + ∠CBD = 90°; in right triangle BCD, ∠CBD + ∠BCD = 90°, therefore ∠ABO = ∠BCD. Thus △ABO and △BCD have two corresponding angles equal, and hypotenuse AB = CB, so △ABO ≅ △BCD. Corresponding sides are equal, obtaining CD = BO = 28 cm. Therefore the distance from point C to the ground is 28 cm.
